steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.

Beat cream cheese in a bowl with an electric mixer until soft and fluffy, then beat in egg until thoroughly combined. Mix in cookie mix, then stir in raspberry chips. Drop the dough about 2 inches apart onto the prepared baking sheets with a tablespoon or small scoop. Lightly pat the cookies to flatten.
Bake cookies in the preheated oven until the edges of the cookies are lightly golden, 10 to 12 minutes. Cool before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Raspberry Cheesecake Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Raspberry cheesecake cookies made with cream cheese, sugar cookie mix, and raspberry baking chips taste just like raspberry cheesecake in cookie form!

review.reviewBody: Amazing! I too could not find raspberry baking chips. In place, I bought a small can of raspberry pie filler. I mixed the ingredients as directed (leaving out the raspberry chips/pie filler) and after mixing was complete I GENTLY folded the filler (about half the can) in with the dough. Roll into balls, slightly flatten. They turned out perfect!

This is my first review and well overdue considering I am a avid stalker of this site and of course a fan of mis7-ups, (one of my favorite cooks). I was excited to try this recipe considering how easy it was along with the few ingredients, but her excitement about the cookie had me so courious that I could not wait for other reviews which is something I would typically never think of doing. As for the recipe...I took my short shopping list to Walmart and of course could not find raspberry baking chips so I had to improvise the recipe slightly. I added & beat in 2 teaspoons of raspberry extract to the egg/cream cheese mixture, then the cookie mix per the instructions..and just because I felt I needed to add something to replace the raspberry chips, I folded in some white chocolate chips. I did not flatten down the cookie dough prior to baking and ended up with 30 cake-cookies. My hubby absolutely LOVED these and took them to work to share, (and brag about my cooking LOL). Mis7-Up thank you for an awesome recipe!
I'm giving it 5 stars because its awesome with white chocolate chips but WHERE does one find raspberry chips??? Please post! ! !

Loved this! Very pretty cookie. Took it to a cookie exchange, and it was a hit. I followed the recipe exactly using this hints from other reviewers. These are the steps I used (following advice from reviewers).

1. Soaked 1/2 cup white chocolate chips in 1/2 teaspoon Raspberry extract overnight for Raspberry (per suggestion). Did not have raspberry bits so used Ocean Spray Cherry Craisons minced up in food processor.

2. Used parchment baking paper on cookie sheet. Used teaspoons coated with butter-flavored Pam to drop on cookie sheet. Used glass coated with Pam to flatten cookies (per suggestion). Sprinkled tops with Wilton White Sparkling Sprinkles for added visual zip. Cooked exactly 10 minutes. Did not look done -BUT THEY WERE!
Have soaked some mini Ghiradelli chocolate chips in raspberry extract to try next. A new keeper!! Thanks mis7up!

My version: I used a cinnamon sugar cookie mix with white chips and vanilla extract. I needed to finish mixing by hand while adding the chips, since it was so thick. I put them on silpat sheets which helped since the dough was so sticky. I dropped clumps of dough on, put them in the fridge for a few minutes and then rolled them into balls and flattened them. That really helped to form them into round cookies. They are very cake-like. The sheet of cookies that were on the top rack in the oven came out puffier and the chips were more melted. I put them in a minute later and then moved them to the bottom rack for another two minutes and turned them down to 325. Interesting taste, not too sweet; the kids said the bottom rack ones were tastier, although they don't look as nice and look still doughy, while the bottoms are brown. A fun recipe to experiment with - what is your version?

Very delicious. I have trouble finding the raspberry chips also but here is how you fix that dilemma. Place 2 cups semi sweet chocolate chips into a plastic zip log bag with 1/4 t. raspberry extract. Let sit 24 hours and they are ready to use. Don't have 24 hours....use 1/2 t. raspberry extract instead and they are ready immediately. I usually have a bag of these going all the time. You can also do this for the mint chocolate chips. Have been doing this for years. Enjoy!
I usually find the raspberry extract at specialty bakery stores that carry all the baking special needs.

THESE COOKIES ARE DANGEROUS!! I got the 'tidbits' on sale from Prepared Pantry website last Friday, and made these twice already! One 12 oz bag makes 4+ batches. The 2nd time around, I rolled by hand like thumbprints and flattened slightly with my fingers. These turned out the best based on cooking time given. I even left the second sheet in for 10 extra minutes (got sidetracked outside talking to neighbors) and they just would not burn! AWESOME! LOVED BY ALL. I may try adding a dab of lemon juice next time for real cheesecake flavor! Oh, I also sprayed parchment and tips of cookies with Pam and this helped to brown SLIGHTLY! A real hit at my home!

ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE! I love the "hit" of raspberry in this delicious cookie. I also discovered I am married to a cookie monster! This cookie not only tastes good, it is pretty to look at. As I could never find the raspberry chips, I decided to make my own. I used 2/3 cup white chocolate, 1/4 tsp. raspberry extract, red food coloring and a little shortening. I piped the morsels using a zip lock bag onto parchment paper. A few minutes in the refrigerator and they were good to go. The cookies were so easy to make. I found baking 12 minutes worked for me. (note to self for next time). Thank you mis7up for such an ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE cookie!

No one at my house I really a big fan of raspberries so I used sour apple chips and it was yummy. Also I used fat free organic creme cheese which prolongs the baking time a bit but brings the calorie count down a bit as well. For easy transport I baked them in little baking cups.

Just made these last night and they were great! But I modified the recipe because I didn't find the raspberry chips. Instead I used raspberry preserves, about 1/3 of a cup, and white chocolate chips. They were delicious but I am going to bake them longer than I did. I baked them for 24 minutes because at 12 minutes they were still very raw. I think I might up it to 35 minutes because even after that they are still pretty soft...

WOW. These may very well be the most delicious cookies I've ever had. They're seriously incredible.

I ordered the raspberry baking chips (officially called Raspberry Tidbits) from Amazon. I very highly recommend using these rather than a substitution. I also used Renewal Mill upcycled sugar cookie mix (15 oz package). Baked for 12 minutes, which was perfect.

I look forward to sharing these with everyone I know and also experimenting with the recipe! Some chocolate chips would be a great addition.
The chunks of cream cheese really ruined this recipe. Maybe creamy instead of chunks?

I was excited to see two of my favorite flavors, cheesecake and raspberry in a cookie. I was extremely disappointed! These were fairly dry and tasteless and for the yield, quite expensive to make as the raspberry had to be ordered. Also wasted a block of cream cheese and the cookie mix which by itself is usually ok. the only positive is they are easy but no way would I make them again....
I used cherry flavored baking chips because I couldn't find raspberry. They came out great!

I love this recipe and get tons of compliments every time I make it. Re: where to find raspberry baking chips, I go to the Prepared Pantry website. They are called "Raspberry Tidbits" (Gourmet Fruit Baking Chips) and taste like real raspberries, minus the sogginess of real ones! You will only need to add 1/3 to 1/2 of the tidbits package for the recipe. I also add white chocolate chips.

I ordered raspberry tidbits from Amazon and they mistakenly sent me blueberry tidbits! I was wanting to make these cookies and didn’t want to wait until the replacement of raspberry tidbits arrived. So I went with the blueberry ones. Delicious and so easy and quick to make. Can’t wait to make them with the raspberry ones! Thanks for the recipe, Melissa!
First of. it takes oven 375*. took 10min. to bake

I made this recipe but added in 1 1/2 Cup of White Chocolate Chips to mimic the Raspberry Cheesecake cookies from Subway. They weren't quite the same but were still super yummy! 
PS. If you're having trouble finding the Raspberry Chips look on Amazon. That's were I found mine.
I made these multiple times now, I make them in raspberry, strawberry, and blueberry. I have been getting requests for these lately. What a great and easy recipe to make.

As many other reviewers mentioned. I also wasn’t able to find raspberry chips. I solved that by chopping some red vanilla melting wafers, and adding 1 tsp raspberry flavoring. The cookies turned out great. Next time I ll add a bit more of the flavoring. Delicious cookies!
